the age-related decrease of GABAAR mRNA expression in the rat cerebrum and cerebellum is not accompanied by a parallel change in GABAAR protein expression, suggesting a complex regulatory mechanisms of receptor expression at the transcriptional and translational levels.

aging leads to significant changes in GABAAR subunits expression in the cerebellar cortex and the cerebral cortex of the rat, and that the expression changes are not necessarily reflected at the protein and functional levels.
aging is associated with decreased expression of GABAA receptors subunits in the rat cerebella and cerebral cortex, but not in the hippocampus.

the study of GABAergic system in the aging brain.
the study of the molecular and cellular mechanisms involved in the age-related changes in GABAA receptor function.
the age-related changes in expression of GABAAR subunits and their functional consequences.

GABAA receptor mRNA and protein expression changes are not necessarily parallel and that the age-related changes in GABAA receptor protein expression are not necessarily reflected by the changes in receptor binding properties.
the GABAA receptor system is not altered in the aged rat cerebellum but that the GABAR system is altered in the aged cerebral cortex.
aging-related changes in GABAA receptor gene expression are complex and region-specific and do not always lead to similar changes at the receptor level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

aging is associated with a decrease in the expression of various GABAA receptor mRNAs and proteins in the rat cerebella and cerebral cortices, and that the age-related changes in GABAA receptor protein expression are not necessarily correlated to changes in GABAR mRNA expression.

the aging-related decreased expression for the GABAAR subunits alpha 1, beta 2/ 3 and gamma 2 is not associated with changes in the assembly of GABAA receptors in the rat cerebrocortical and cerebellar areas.
aging is a process which is accompanied by significant changes in the expression of the main subunits of the GABAARs.

the age-related changes in mRNA expression of a given subunit are not necessarily paralleled by changes in protein expression or in assembly into mature receptors.
the GABAA receptor is a complex receptor and that its expression is regulated at multiple levels.
the expression of various subunits of the GABAA receptor changes during aging in the brain, but the mechanisms involved are not fully understood.
